answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so an agent’s influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than self-asserted identities. A sybil cluster may resemble a marble island in the graph, but its sparse external cut gives it low conductance; min-cut and transitivity bounds then limit how much trusted mass can enter and cap its aggregate voting weight, provided walk length and seed distribution are fixed. A cipher cannot substitute for those attestations.
